question: Should OpenClaw add a built-in response-level tool confirmation gate, and what deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules should decide allow, require-confirm, deny, and timeout behavior?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing gate, but the permanent policy defines a new security boundary and config contract that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design core gate
options.body: Approve a core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and tests proving existing plugin approvals still compose correctly.

options.title: Keep plugin-only
options.body: Keep core behavior unchanged and require operators to implement contextual approvals through before_tool_call.requireApproval or trusted tool policies, accepting that no built-in same-response confirmation gate exists.

options.title: Defer into broader policy work
options.body: Wait for the related action-level deny, pre-response gate, and HITL interrupt designs to settle into one authorization model before adding a new config surface.

recommendation.title: Design core gate
recommendation.body: Approve a core design with disabled-by-default config, deterministic risk/current-turn authorization rules, explicit approve/deny/timeout behavior, and tests proving existing plugin approvals still compose correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, core agent execution ordering, and product-level approval UX, and current history routes the central files through steipete.
